st: Mix the cassava flour with [[1 cup]] cold water in a bowl until smooth and lump free.
Bring [[2 cups]] water to a boil in a heavy pot.
Pour in the flour mixture slowly, stirring hard with a wooden spoon.
Cook over medium-low heat for 10 minutes, stirring and pressing the dough, until stiff and shiny.
Shape into smooth balls with a wet spoon or hands. Keep warm.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a pan and cook the onion for 3 minutes. Add the spinach and [[0.5 tsp]] salt and wilt for 3 minutes.
Stir in [[3 tbsp]] peanut butter until creamy.
Serve the gozo with the peanut spinach or a stew.
Mix the ground beef with the grated onion, half the chili, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper. Shape into 18 small meatballs.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the meatballs for 6 minutes, turning, then remove.
Add [[1 tbsp]] oil, the chopped onion and garlic. Cook for 4 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and the remaining chili. Cook for 6 minutes until saucy.
Stir in the ground pumpkin seeds, [[2 cups]] water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Bring to a gentle boil.
Return the meatballs to the sauce. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring gently, until the sauce is thick and the meat is 160°F (71°C).
Serve hot over rice or with cassava dough.
Soak the dried fish in hot water for 15 minutes, then flake and remove bones.
Boil the cassava leaves in [[3 cups]] water for 30 minutes until tender. Do not drain.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] palm oil in a pan and cook the onion and garlic for 4 minutes.
Add the onion mixture, fish, whole chili and [[1 tsp]] salt to the leaves.
Stir [[0.5 cup]] peanut butter with a ladle of the hot cooking liquid until smooth. Pour it into the pot.
Cover and simmer on low for 35 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Remove the whole chili. Taste and adjust the salt.
Serve hot with rice or gozo.

ing: whole tilapia or firm fish fillets
st: Rub the fish with the lemon juice, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper. Rest 10 minutes.
Mix the onion, tomatoes, chili, garlic, [[2 tbsp]] oil and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a bowl.
Soften the banana leaves over a flame or in hot water, then cut into 4 large squares.
Put a share of the fish on each leaf and top with the vegetable mix.
Fold into tight packets and tie with twine, or wrap in foil.
Steam over simmering water for 35 minutes, or bake at 375°F (190°C) for 35 minutes.
Check that the fish is opaque and flakes at 145°F (63°C).
Open the packets carefully and serve with rice or cassava dough.
Season the chicken with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a heavy pot and brown the chicken for 4 minutes per side. Remove to a plate.
Cook the onion and garlic in the same pot for 4 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and whole chili and cook for 6 minutes until soft.
Whisk [[0.75 cup]] peanut butter with [[1 cup]] hot water until smooth, then stir into the pot.
Add the chicken, [[2 cups]] more water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low for 40 minutes, stirring from the bottom so the peanut does not stick, until chicken is 165°F (74°C).
Remove the whole chili. Serve with rice or boiled cassava.
Stir the yeast and [[1 tbsp]] of the sugar into [[1 cup]] warm water. Wait 8 minutes until foamy.
Mix the flour, remaining sugar and salt in a bowl.
Add the yeast water and mix into a thick, sticky dough. Add a splash more water if it is stiff.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour, until doubled.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Wet a spoon and drop in tablespoon-size portions of dough, a few at a time.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until puffy and golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.
